basis: Umbrella disorder defined by abnormal development of bone and cartilage; extraskeletal disease is subtype-dependent.
Hyperostosis with facial palsy in 2/2, hearing impairment in 1/2 and nail dysplasia in 1/2; frequencies derive from a very small cohort.
Premature activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal endocrine axis; central origin does not establish neurologic damage.
Parasitic infection; intestinal, urinary and hepatic injury vary by species and disease stage. No single organ's damage frequency is established at >=30% across this umbrella.
Congenital structural abnormality of a major vein; secondary thrombosis and associated anomalies are not universal.
Cardioencephalomyopathy denotes disease of heart, brain and skeletal muscle; no evidence establishes an additional metabolic mechanism.
Sensory-autonomic neuropathy with characteristic acral ulceration in 4/4 and destructive distal phalangeal osteolysis in 3/3; both are integral mutilating features.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability define the syndrome; obesity and limb hypotonia are only occasional, and facial dysmorphism adds no damaged organ.
Congenital obstruction of pulmonary veins; pulmonary hypertension remains vascular. Respiratory symptoms and recurrent infections do not establish common direct lung injury.
Ancestors and included subtypes identify autoimmune platelet disease, including immune thrombocytopenia and Evans syndrome.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with visual impairment and cardiac malformations each reported in 80-99%; feeding difficulty and constipation alone do not establish intestinal injury.
Muscular dystrophy defines the group; skin fragility and blistering accompany the predominant EBS-muscular dystrophy form (>30%), but not isolated limb-girdle disease.
Renal glomerular dysfunction and neurodevelopmental impairment define the syndrome; isolated additional findings do not establish common injury elsewhere.
Developmental, skeletal and cardiac defects define syndrome; hydronephrosis/reflux occur in 30-79%. Common oral/dental anomalies omitted at four-axis cap.
Mitochondrial encephalopathy with cardiomyopathy; skeletal myopathy is a defining feature in the supplied synonyms, meeting the diagnostic-feature exception.
Corneal disorder, muscular atrophy and nephropathy are defining components supported by synonyms and ancestors; no additional mechanism inferred.
Hereditary abnormality of epidermal appendages; extracutaneous involvement varies among subtypes.
Zellweger-spectrum disorder: neurologic dysfunction, liver disease and retinal degeneration commonly exceed 30%; hearing loss also common, omitted at four-axis cap.
Neurodevelopmental syndrome; visual dysfunction/strabismus and gastrointestinal dysmotility each occur in 30-79%. External-ear shape alone does not establish ear dysfunction.
Staphylococcal infection umbrella spans multiple anatomical sites; no particular organ is consistently affected across the group.
Inherited retinal and macular degeneration causing reduced visual acuity.
Generalized hyperostosis causes facial nerve palsy and sensorineural hearing loss, each in 30-79%; optic atrophy lacks evidence of >=30% frequency.
Genetic focal epilepsy and associated neurodevelopmental dysfunction affect the nervous system.
Paroxysmal movement disorder with dystonia and involuntary movements; abnormal movements do not establish primary skeletal-muscle damage.
Autosomal dominant nonsyndromic hearing loss; no extra-auditory disease is established.
